title: GCSE Biology | Exam-Style Questions Bank (BBC Bitesize)

questions.stem: The diagram shows the main components of an animal cell. State the name of the part of the cell that is the site of respiration.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the site of respiration in animal (and plant) cells. Cells which need more energy like muscle cells, have more mitochondria. The cytoplasm is a jelly-like material where many chemical reactions occur. The nucleus contains genetic material, including DNA, which controls the cell's activities. Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis (where proteins are made). The cell membrane surrounds the cell and controls what enters and leaves it.

questions.stem: Many exchange surfaces in living things have a large surface area. Select the correct example of an exchange surface.

options.C: The villi in the digestive system

questions.explanation: The villi in the digestive system is the correct example of exchange surfaces with a large surface area. The elongated (long length) axons in neurones helps impulses pass along them quickly. These are not exchange surfaces. The flagella of some bacteria allow them to move. These are not exchange surfaces. The ciliated cells lining oviduct have tiny hairs (cilia) which beat regularly to move the egg from the ovary to the uterus. These are not exchange surfaces.

questions.stem: Communicable diseases, like the common cold, can infect organisms in different ways. Select the correct way in which many farmers believe tuberculosis infects their cows.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is that many farmers believe that tuberculosis is spread by badgers to their cows. Organisms that spread communicable diseases are called vectors. The malaria mosquito transmits this disease from the blood of infected people to those that are not infected. Direct contact transmits some communicable diseases between people, but not tuberculosis. Direct contact can be sexual or non-sexual touching. Untreated water can transmit many diseases, such as the cholera bacterium but again not tuberculosis. Coughs and sneezes can transmit communicable diseases like the common cold thro

questions.stem: Glucose is produced by plants when they photosynthesise. This is used to build larger substances within plants. Which substances are made by joining glucose and nitrates from the soil?
questions.explanation: Amino acids are the substances that are made by joining glucose and nitrates from the soil. Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins which are made when they join together in the correct sequence. Lipids are fats (solid at room temperature) and oils (liquids under the same conditions). Glucose is stored as lipids in plant seeds. We make sunflower oil from sunflower seeds. Many molecules of glucose made in photosynthesis are joined together to make starch which is a storage form of carbohydrate found in rice, cereals and potatoes. Many molecules of glucose are joined together to make cel

questions.stem: State the name of the cells in your nervous system which detect stimuli and make electrical signals which travel towards the central nervous system.
questions.explanation: Receptor cells detect stimuli, which are changes in the environment. You have receptors in all of your sense organs, and temperature, pressure and pain receptors in your skin. They detect changes and send electrical signals along nerves to your brain. Effectors are muscles or glands at the end of your motor neurones. They respond to signals sent from your central nervous system. Muscles move parts of your body, and glands release hormones (which are chemical signals) into your blood. Nerves are made from bundles of individual neurone cells.

questions.stem: Mitosis is part of the cell cycle. State the name of the stage in mitosis when chromosomes and their copies line up in the middle of a cell.
questions.explanation: The stages of mitosis in which chromosomes and their copies line up in the middle of a cell is called metaphase. The first stage in mitosis is for the DNA in the cell, which is arranged into chromosomes, to condense and become more visible. This occurs in prophase, where the membrane around the nucleus also disappears. Telophase happens before this when new membranes form around the chromosomes at each end of the cells. Finally the cell splits into two genetically identical cells during cytokinesis.

questions.stem: All animals and plants compete with each other for resources. This can either be interspecific or intraspecific. Select the answer which describes an example of intraspecific competition.

options.A: Zebras and gazelles grazing on grassland
options.B: Magpies and red kite birds feeding on a dead pheasant
options.C: Young oak trees growing from acorns dropped under a mature oak tree
options.D: Mice and rats eating the grain stored by a farmer

questions.explanation: Competition for resources between individuals of the same species is called intraspecific. 'Intra' in science means 'within' so this competition is within one species. The correct example is therefore young oak trees (one species) seeking light under their parent tree. Competition for resources between individuals of different species is called interspecific. 'Inter' in science means 'between' so this competition is between different species. Examples of this are zebras and gazelle (different species) grazing on grass, magpies and red kites (different species) feeding on roadkill, and rats and

questions.stem: Microscopes are used to magnify samples. What is the scientific name of the part of the microscope that can be used to change the magnification?
questions.explanation: It is the objective lenses that can easily be changed to alter the magnification. The highest magnification objective lens is often x40. The eyepiece lens cannot easily be changed. This is often x10 on a light microscope. The condenser ensures light is spread uniformly over the slide you are looking at. The coarse focus allows you to quickly find near to the perfect focus, which you can then find using the fine focus.

questions.stem: An example of a woodland food chain can be seen above.The caterpillars contains 12000 kJ of energy. Ten percent of this is transferred to each additional level in the food chain.Calculate the energy transferred to the owl.
questions.explanation: A further 10% (120 kJ), is then passed to the owl. 120000 kJ is the energy that is in the oak tree. 10800 kJ is 90% of the energy that will be in the caterpillars not the 10% that is passed on. 1200 kJ is the energy within the shrews.

questions.stem: Smaller animals like mice have a much larger surface area to volume ratio. Larger animals like elephants have a smaller surface area to volume ratio.The image above shows the surface area (SA), volume (Vol) and ratio between the surface area and volume (SA:Vol) for 1 cm and 2 cm cubes.Calculate the surface area and volume of the 3 cm cube. Give your answer as a ratio.
questions.explanation: Each face is 9 cm² and there are six faces on a cube. So the surface area is 9 x 6 = 54 cm² There are nine cubes on each of the three layers so the volume is 9 x 3 = 27cm³ The ratio between these two numbers is 2:1

questions.stem: Specialised animal and plant cells have adaptations to allow them to fulfil their specific roles.Select the adaptation of a palisade mesophyll cell.

options.A: They have spaces between them to allow air to circulate
options.B: They open and close to allow gases to enter the leaf
options.C: They transport the products of photosynthesis around the plant
options.D: They contain many chloroplasts to carry out photosynthesis

questions.explanation: Palisade mesophyll cells are adapted to carry out photosynthesis by having many chloroplasts, which is where photosynthesis occurs. Spongy mesophyll cells have spaces between them to allow gases to circulate and reach all cells in the leaf. Guard cells that surround stomata open and close to allow gases to enter the leaves. Phloem cells transport the products of photosynthesis, including sugars and amino acids, around the plant.

questions.stem: Your digestive system breaks down large insoluble molecules in your food into smaller soluble ones which can be absorbed.State where the digestion of proteins occurs.
questions.explanation: The only places in the digestive system where proteins are broken down into amino acids are the stomach and small intestine. Protease enzymes catalyse these reactions. Carbohydrates are broken down by carbohydrase enzymes in the mouth, pancreas and small intestine. Lipids are broken down in the small intestine. The pancreas produces enzymes to break down proteins, carbohydrates and lipids but this digestion occurs in the small intestine and not the pancreas itself.

questions.stem: Identify the correct statement about the immune system.

options.A: Red blood cells in your blood fight infection
options.B: White blood cells produce antigens which clump pathogens together
options.C: A second exposure to a pathogen or vaccine produces more antibodies faster
options.D: Herd immunity stops all transmission of a disease

questions.explanation: This graph shows a second exposure just before day 20. The increase in antibodies afterwards is steeper meaning more antibodies are produced faster. It is white blood cells in your blood which fight infection. These cells engulf and destroy pathogens or produce proteins called antibodies (not antigens) which are the correct shape to clump pathogens together. Their shape matches proteins called antigens on the surface of the pathogen.

questions.stem: Respiration releases energy for cells to complete life processes.State the product or products of anaerobic respiration.
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration occurs without sufficient oxygen. So the only product of anaerobic respiration is lactic acid. Carbon dioxide and water are the products of aerobic respiration which occurs in the presence of oxygen. Glucose and oxygen are the products of photosynthesis and the reactants in aerobic respiration. Glucose alone is the reactant of anaerobic respiration.

questions.stem: Hormones are chemical messages produced in glands that travel in the bloodstream.Select the correct location of your body's pituitary gland and its effect.

options.A: In the brain and controls other glands
options.B: Above the kidneys and increases heart rate
options.C: In the throat and controls metabolism
options.D: In the abdomen and lowers blood sugar

questions.explanation: The pituitary gland is in the brain. It produces several hormones which act upon other glands to stimulate further hormones to be produced. It is called the 'master gland'. The adrenal glands are found above your kidneys. They release the hormone adrenaline which increases your heart rate for a flight, flight or freeze response. The thyroid gland is in the throat. This produces the hormone thyroxine which controls your metabolism. The pancreas is found in the abdomen. It produces insulin and glucagon which regulate blood sugar.

questions.stem: Select the piece of equipment that you would use to sample small insects.
questions.explanation: Pooters are small pieces of equipment that allow you to suck small insects into a jar without touching them. A small piece of mesh stops you breathing them in. Sweep nets are swept through long grass, as you walk slowly through it, to catch flying insects. Quadrats are square frames which are placed randomly or systematically in a habitat to record the number of plants or slow moving animals within them. A transect is an imaginary line that is drawn across a habitat to systematically sample a habitat. They are not actually a piece of equipment.

questions.stem: The ability to roll your tongue is controlled by a single dominant gene.Two heterozygous parents for tongue rolling decide to have a child.Calculate the chance of their child not being able to roll their tongue.
questions.explanation: We can display the information above in a Punnett table genetic cross (above). The genes of the two parents are shown in red. They are both heterozygous for tongue rolling which means they have both inherited T from one of their parents and t from the other. Because tongue rolling is a dominant gene, both TT and Tt can roll their tongues, and only tt cannot. The cross shows that there is a one in four chance of them having a child which is tt. This is 25 % or a probability of 0.25

questions.stem: Food tests allow scientists to see if particular substances are present in foods.State the name of the reagent that reacts with reducing sugars and the colour change expected.
questions.explanation: Benedict's reagent is used to test for reducing sugars and the sample will turn green, orange or red if they are present. Biuret solution is the reagent when testing for protein. A sample will turn purple if protein is present. Iodine is the test for starch. A sample will turn black or blue if starch is present.

questions.stem: State the name of the scientist who developed the theory of evolution by natural section independently of Charles Darwin.
questions.explanation: Alfred Wallace developed the theory of evolution by natural selection independently of Charles Darwin but shortly after him. He is also known for his work on speciation. Jean-Baptiste Lamarck incorrectly stated (in the majority of cases) that a characteristic that is used more by an organism within its lifetime becomes bigger or stronger and is passed on to offspring. James Watson worked with Francis Crick and Rosalind Franklin to discover the structure of DNA. Edward Jenner developed the first vaccination. He exposed milkmaids to cowpox which prevented them from catching the more serious smal

questions.stem: A student is looking at human cheek cells using a light microscope.The size of the cell in the image is 20mm. The magnification is x400.Rearrange the equation above to calculate the real size of the cell in millimetres.
questions.explanation: The first step is to rearrange the equation to be: Real size of object = size of image ÷ magnification So the calculation is: Real size of object = 20 ÷ 400 Which makes the answer 0.05 mm. 50 is the incorrect answer given in micrometres not millimetres. 8000 is the incorrect answer if you multiply 20 and 400, not divide one by the other. 20 is the incorrect answer if you divided 400 by 20 and not the other way around.

questions.stem: Genes are passed from parents to their offspring. Select the correct definition of a gene.

options.A: The material inside the nucleus of cells which carries the genetic information of the organism.
options.B: The basic unit of genetic material inherited from our parents.
options.C: An x-shaped thread-like structure made from DNA which codes for all the genetic characteristics of an organism.
options.D: One copy of all of the DNA of an organism.

questions.explanation: A gene is defined as the basic unit of genetic material inherited from our parents. The material inside the nucleus of cells which carries the genetic information of the organism is called DNA. Chromosomes are x-shaped thread-like structures made from DNA. One copy of all of the DNA of an organism is called its genome.

questions.stem: Transpiration is the continual loss of water from leaves by evaporation through the stomata. Under which conditions is this process least likely to occur?

options.A: Low humidity, low temperature and windy
options.B: High humidity, low temperature and still
options.C: High humidity, high temperature and still
options.D: Low humidity, high temperature and windy

questions.explanation: Transpiration is slowest when there is high humidity and so the concentration of water in the air inside the leaf and outside the leaf are similar. It is also slowest when the temperature is low because molecular movement is also slow. Finally still air means any evaporated water can remain closer to the leaf rather than being blown away. This again means the concentration inside and out remain more similar reducing the rate.

questions.stem: The human body has a number of defences against infection by pathogens. These can be chemical or physical. Select the physical defence from the list below.
questions.explanation: Scabs are a form of physical defence formed when your skin is cut to stop infecting pathogens. Stomach acid is a chemical form of defence which kills pathogens in food or drink. Enzymes in tears are also a chemical form of defence which stop infections in eyes. Lysozymes are a type of enzyme found in saliva, breast milk and mucus which stop infections and so are therefore another chemical form of defence.

questions.stem: A limiting factor is something that can slow the rate of a reaction if it is not present. Which of these is not an example of a limiting factor in photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Glucose is not a limiting factor because it is a product and not a reactant. If there is not enough carbon dioxide then this is a limiting factor because it slows the rate of photosynthesis. Photosynthesis occurs in plant cells which contain chlorophyll so if there is not enough of this it will also be a limiting factor. Photosynthesis requires light so if the intensity is not high enough this is also a limiting factor.

questions.stem: Body temperature in humans is 37oC. Which of these responses reduces body temperature?
questions.explanation: Vasodilation occurs when you are too hot. The blood vessels near the surface of your skin (called arterioles) widen and so more blood flows to the capillaries in your skin. This allows more heat to be lost to the environment to cool you down. Vasoconstriction occurs when you are too cold. The blood vessels near the surface of your skin (called arterioles) become smaller (constrict) and so less blood flows to your skin. This allows less heat to be lost to the environment to keep you warm. Shivering is the involuntary shaking of skeletal muscles. This generates heat to warm you up. Erector muscl

questions.stem: The first classification system involving the five kingdoms was proposed by Carl Linnaeus in the eighteenth century. More recently, Carl Woose has suggested the three domain system. What evidence did he use?
questions.explanation: Carl Woose used DNA analysis to compare the similarities and differences between the DNA of species. This is more accurate than human judgement which was used previously. Light microscopes have been used for hundreds of years. They were used to look at cells of organisms before the three domain system was proposed. Organisms from previously unknown countries have occasionally been difficult to classify, but they were not used as evidence to move from the five kingdom to the three domain model. The internet was used by Carl Woose and colleagues in their development of the three domain system, b

questions.stem: Food webs show the interdependence of organisms in a habitat. Which of these options correctly describes what would happen if all the frogs were killed?

options.A: The number of foxes and hawks would increase. The number of thrushes and voles would decrease.
options.B: The amount of grass would increase together with the rabbits and slugs.
options.C: The number of insects would increase. The number of foxes would decrease. The number of rabbits would increase.
options.D: The number of insects would decrease together with the number of voles.

questions.explanation: The frogs eat insects and so if the frogs were removed, the number of insects would increase. Frogs are eaten by foxes and hawks and so if their numbers reduced, so would the number of foxes and hawks. If there are fewer foxes then the number of rabbits would increase. If the numbers of an organism in a food chain are reduced, the numbers of those that feed upon it generally decrease as well. In contrast, the number of organisms upon which it feeds usually increases. It is important to remember that interdependence in food chains means that small changes eventually balance out and the populati

questions.stem: Two students were investigating the effects of caffeine on reaction times using the ruler drop test. Their results are below. Calculate the mean result for student A before and after they drank a caffeinated drink. Ignore any anomalous readings and give your answers to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: The first step in this answer is to identify the anomalous (odd) reading. This is reading 4 for student A before caffeine. It is anomalous because it is so far from the others. This is ignored when calculating the mean. The mean is calculated by adding the numbers together and dividing by the number of numbers. For before caffeine this is: (14 + 16 + 18) ÷ 3 = 16 For after caffeine this is: (11 + 14 + 12 + 12) ÷ 4 = 12.3 The value 13.25 is incorrectly calculated if you do not ignore the anomalous reading. The incorrect equivalent values for student B are 20.8 and 18.6

questions.stem: The graph shows the repeated increasing and decreasing of predator and prey cycling. Select the example which best explains what is happening where the label A is pointing.

options.A: The prey are decreasing because the predators are decreasing
options.B: The predators are decreasing because the prey population is very low
options.C: The prey are decreasing because they are being eaten by more predators

questions.explanation: Point A is pointing to the line for the predators. This line is almost always below the prey because there are usually fewer prey than predators. At the point that the label A is pointing, the predator numbers are decreasing because of a reduction in prey. If there is not sufficient food for all the predators to eat then some will die and their numbers will reduce.

questions.stem: Chlamydia is a sexually transmitted disease. The number of people diagnosed with Chlamydia in England changed from 202,178 in 2015 to 159,448 in 2021. Calculate the rate of change of infection. Give your answer to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: The change in number of infections is 159,448 - 202,178 = -42,730 You then work out the rate of change by dividing by the change in time (6 years):-42,730 ÷ 6 (years) = -7121.7 This is the rate of change per year.

questions.stem: The melting and boiling points of some of the halogens are shown in the table. Which of these options is the best prediction for the melting point and boiling point of bromine?
questions.explanation: There is a clear trend in the melting points in the table, so choose a value which is approximately halfway between chlorine and iodine - which would be around -7 A melting point of 89 would be far too high - too similar to the melting point of iodine. The trend in boiling points is similar. Choosing a value for the boiling point which is around halfway between chlorine and iodine would be sensible, and that would be at exactly 75 Given a choice in the question between 59 and 12, 59 is the more sensible choice because it is closerto 75. An answer of 12 seems too close to the boiling point of c

questions.stem: What name is given to a giant structure of carbon atoms where each atom is covalently bonded to three others in a single layer?
questions.explanation: A single layer of carbon atoms where each one is covalently bonded to three others is called graphene. Graphite is a giant covalent structure which is made from millions of these layers stacked on top of each other. Buckminsterfullerene has the formula C60 and it is made from spheres of carbon atoms. Carbon nanotubes are very longandthin cylinders which can be thought of as sheets of graphene rolled up into tubes.

questions.stem: Which of the following equations has been correctly balanced?
questions.explanation: It is important to carefully count each type of atom present before the reaction (to the left of the arrow) and after the reaction (on the right of the arrow) to make sure that an equation is balanced. Equations must be balanced, because atoms cannot be created or destroyed in chemical reactions. The reaction 2CH₃OH + 3O₂ →2CO₂ + 4H₂O has 2 C atoms, 8 H atoms and 8 O atoms on both sides, so it is balanced. The reaction CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O has 4 H atoms on the left but only 2 on the right. The reaction Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe has one Al atom on the left but 2 on the right. The reaction 2NaOH

questions.stem: Using the reactivity series in the diagram, which metal could be extracted from its oxide ore by heating the ore with carbon in a displacement reaction?
questions.explanation: Zinc can be extracted from zinc oxide by heating with carbon because zinc is less reactive than carbon. This means that the carbon will displace the zinc: Carbon + zinc oxide → zinc + carbon dioxide Gold is typically found in rocks as the metal element itself, rather than being bonded to oxygen or other elements, so does not need to be heated with carbon. Aluminium and calcium cannot be extracted by heating their oxides with carbon. Carbon is less reactive than aluminium and calcium so it cannot displace these elements.

questions.stem: A student investigated energy changes during some chemical reactions. The apparatus they used is shown in the diagram.

options.B: Repeat the experiment three times and calculate a mean temperature change
options.D: Ask another student to repeat the experiment using slightly different equipment

questions.explanation: Using an insulating lid will reduce the unwanted heat transfers between the reaction mixture and the surroundings. This will improve the accuracy of the results. Measurements are accurate if they are close to the true value. Repeating the measurements and ignoring anomalous results before calculating a mean temperature will check to see if the results are repeatable. Asking another student to repeat the experiment is a way to see if the results are reproducible.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about dynamic equilibrium is false?

options.B: The reaction must take place in a sealed container
options.C: The rates of the forwards and reverse reactions must be equal

questions.explanation: When a reversible reaction takes place within a closed system (a sealed container) a dynamic equilibrium will occur when the rate of the forwards reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction. During a dynamic equilibrium, the reaction has not stopped, but the speed at which the reactants are making the products is equal to the speed at which the products are turning back into the reactants. This means that the amount of products remains constant over time.

questions.stem: A student was given a sample of hexane and a sample of hexene. How can she identify which is which?

options.A: Dip some damp litmus paper into the samples. Hexene will bleach it white
options.B: Shake the samples with bromine water. The hexene will turn it from orange to colourless
options.C: Shake the samples with limewater. The hexene will turn it from colourless to milky
options.D: Dip a piece of universal indicator into each sample. Hexene will turn it red and hexane will turn it purple

questions.explanation: Bromine water is used to test for an alkene (like hexene). Bromine water changes colour from orange to colourless when it is shaken with an alkene. Damp litmus paper will be bleached to white by chlorine gas. Limewater will turn milky (cloudy) when it is shaken with carbon dioxide gas. Universal indicator paper will turn red in acidic solutions and purple in alkaline solutions. Neither hexene nor hexane are acidic nor alkaline.

questions.stem: Whilst investigating which pigments were present in a coloured ink, a student set up the chromatography experiment as shown in the diagram.

options.A: There is no lid on the beaker
options.B: The solvent level is too high
options.C: More than one spot has been placed on the start line
options.D: The start line should be drawn in pencil

questions.explanation: In chromatography, the start line must be drawn in pencil. If it is drawn in pen, it is likely to rise up the paper and separate out into different pigments, which will ruin the experiment. Whilst a lid is often used to prevent some solvents from evaporating, water doesn't evaporate very quickly so a lid isn't necessary. This is not an error. The solvent level must be below the start line at the beginning of the experiment, as shown in the diagram, so this is not an error. It is normal for the start line to have more than one spot, so that a mixture can be compared with individual pure pigment

questions.stem: Individual people can make lifestyle choices which can reduce their carbon footprint.

options.B: Eating more rice instead of wheat-based foods
options.D: Collecting litter from a local park

questions.explanation: Meat based diets have a higher carbon footprint than plant based (vegan) diets. This is because farming animals causes the release of greenhouse gases. For example, farming cows releases methane. Farming rice in paddy fields also releases methane, which is a powerful greenhouse gas. Increasing electricity consumption at home will increase a person's carbon footprint because at the moment, much of the UK's electricity is generated by burning fossil fuels and this releases carbon dioxide. Collecting litter from a local park is a good thing to do because litter can be harmful to plants and animal

questions.stem: Which of the following is widely used as a source of drinking water in the UK?
questions.explanation: In the UK, drinking water is obtained from lakes or rivers, or from water that has collected underground. These underground water sources are called aquifers. Sewage is processed to make it safe to return to rivers, but it is not usually processed directly to make it safe to drink. Plants are not used as a source of drinking water. Sea water is not widely used in the UK to produce drinking water. Removing the salt from sea water is called desalination and it requires a lot of energy, either through distillation or reverse osmosis. This would make the process very expensive.

questions.stem: The boat in the image above is moving forwards, and has multiple forces acting on it. Determine the resultant force acting on the boat and state how it will affect the boat's motion.

options.A: The resultant force is 800 N forwards, and the boat will accelerate
options.B: The resultant force is 800 N forwards, and the boat will decelerate
options.C: The resultant force is 600 N forwards, and the boat will accelerate
options.D: The resultant force is 600N forwards, and the boat will decelerate

questions.explanation: To find the resultant force, all the forces acting on an object are combined, to give a single force. The forces acting upwards (upthrust) and downwards (weight) are equal so they cancel out, and there is no resultant force in the vertical direction. This means the resultant force is determined by subtracting the backwards force (drag) from the forwards force (thrust): Resultant force = 800 - 200 = 600 N The force is in the same direction as the motion of the boat, so this causes the boat to accelerate. Option 1 is incorrect because the resultant force is 600 N forwards, not 800 N. Option 2 is

questions.stem: The diagram shows the electromagnetic spectrum. State the names of the electromagnetic waves in the sections of the diagram labelled 1 and 2

options.A: The region labelled 1 is ultraviolet radiation and the region labelled 2 is microwaves
options.B: The region labelled 1 is microwaves and the region labelled 2 is ultraviolet radiation
options.C: The region labelled 1 is ultrasound waves. and the region labelled 2 is sound waves
options.D: The region labelled 1 is sound waves. and the region labelled 2 is ultrasound waves

questions.explanation: Microwaves are electromagnetic waves with frequencies which are higher than radio waves, but lower than infrared radiation. Ultraviolet radiation has frequencies which are higher than visible light, but lower than X-rays. Option A is incorrect because the region labelled 1 represents microwaves, not ultraviolet - and the region labelled 2 represents ultraviolet, not microwaves. Options C and D are incorrect because sound waves and ultrasound waves are not types of electromagnetic wave.

questions.stem: The trolley in the diagram above is moving in a forwards direction. Calculate the momentum of the blue trolley.
questions.explanation: The momentum of the blue trolley can be calculated by substituting the correct values of mass and velocity into the equation: p = m × v p = 2 × 3 p = 6 kg m/s Option 1 is incorrect because the mass has been divided by the velocity, instead of being multiplied by the velocity. Option 2 is incorrect because the velocity has been divided by the mass, instead of being multiplied by the mass. Option 4 is incorrect because it gives the energy in the trolley's kinetic store, instead of the momentum.

questions.stem: The diagram shows the seven regions of the electromagnetic (EM) spectrum. Which types of EM wave could damage cells, causing a cancer to develop inside the body?
questions.explanation: X-rays and gamma rays are ionising radiation which can damage the DNA in the nucleus of cells. This can cause cancers to develop inside the body. Option 1 is incorrect because microwave radiation is not ionising, so cannot damage DNA - and hence does not cause cancers to develop. Option 3 is incorrect because ultraviolet radiation is absorbed by the skin, so can only damage the DNA in skin cells. This means it can cause skin cancer, but cannot cause cancers to develop inside the body. Option 4 is incorrect because neither microwaves nor infrared radiation are ionising - so they do not cause ca

questions.stem: A cyclist takes 4 seconds to accelerate from 7 m/s to 12 m/s. Calculate the cyclist's acceleration.
questions.explanation: The acceleration of the cyclist can be calculated by substituting the correct values of change in velocity and time taken into the equation. Note that the change in velocity is found by subtracting the cyclist's initial velocity from their final velocity. a = Δv ÷ t a = (12 - 7) ÷ 4 a = 5 ÷ 4 a = 1.25 m/s² Option 1 is incorrect because the final velocity has been divided by the time taken, instead of dividing the change in velocity by the surface area. Option 2 is incorrect because the initial velocity has been divided by the time taken, instead of dividing the change in velocity by the surfac

questions.stem: The lamp in the circuit above has a p.d. of 6 V across it, and a current of 1.75 A. Calculate the power dissipated by the lamp.
questions.explanation: The power of the lamp can be calculated by substituting the correct values of potential difference and current into the equation: P = V x I P = 6 × 1.75 P = 10.5 W Option 1 is incorrect because the potential difference has been divided by the current, instead of being multiplied by the current. Option 2 is incorrect because the current has been subtracted from the p.d., instead of dividing the p.d. by the current. Option 3 is incorrect because the potential difference has been added to the current, instead of being divided by the current.

questions.stem: The immersion heater in the diagram is used to heat a block of metal. It has a power of 50 W and is switched on for 10 minutes. Calculate the energy transferred to the heater.
questions.explanation: The energy transferred can be calculated by rearranging the equation to make E (energy transferred) the subject, and then substituting the correct values of change in velocity and time taken into the formula. Note that the time needs to be converted from minutes into seconds first. E = P × t E = 50 × 600 E = 30,000 J Option 1 is incorrect because the power has been divided by the time taken, instead of being multiplied by the time taken. Option 2 is incorrect because the power has been divided by the time taken, instead of being multiplied by the time taken. Option 3 is incorrect because the t

questions.stem: A student inflates a balloon. After leaving the balloon in a cold area, they notice it has partially deflated. Which statement correctly describes the reason why?

options.A: The temperature of the balloon has decreased, causing the air particles to move more slowly and collide with the walls of the balloon less frequently - so the pressure decreases
options.B: The temperature of the balloon has decreased, causing the air particles to move more quickly and collide with the walls of the balloon more frequently - so the pressure decreases
